a.d: Used when the speaker devoted continuous time and effort to an intentional action, causing a negative consequence or inability to do something else.
ex: 시험공부를 **하느라고** 잠을 못 잤어요. / I couldn't sleep because I was studying for the exam.

b.d: A neutral, general cause that can describe states, natural phenomena, or positive outcomes.
ex: 열심히 공부**해서** 시험에 합격했어요. / I passed the exam because I studied hard.

im-02-02-01.tip: -느라고 can only be used with active verbs and negative results, never with positive results or adjectives.

im-02-02-01.q: Fix the unnatural use of -느라고 with a positive outcome.
im-02-02-01.hint: -느라고 can only lead to negative or burdensome results. For a positive achievement, use -어서/아서: 공부해서 장학금을 받았어요.
im-02-02-01.why: -느라고 cannot be followed by a positive achievement like receiving a scholarship. Use -아서/어서 instead.

im-02-02-02.h: Regular Attachment vs ㄹ-Drop Verbs with -느라고

a.d: Directly attach -느라고 to the verb stem without tense markers (no -았/었-).
ex: 책을 **읽느라고** 연락을 못 봤어요. / I missed the message because I was reading a book.

b.d: When verbs end with ㄹ batchim, the final ㄹ drops before -느라고 (만들다 → 만드느라고, 놀다 → 노느라고).
ex: 선물을 **만드느라고** 밤을 새웠어요. / I stayed up all night making a gift.

im-02-02-02.tip: Never attach tense markers to -느라고 (did X = 하느라고, NOT 했느라고). Drop ㄹ for stems ending in ㄹ.

im-02-02-02.q: Fix the tense insertion error before -느라고.
im-02-02-02.wrong: 어제 친구들과 놀았느라고 과제를 못 냈어요.
answers: 어제 친구들과 노느라고 과제를 못 냈어요.
어제 친구들과 노느라고 과제를 못 냈어요
im-02-02-02.hint: -느라고 cannot take past tense -았/었-, and 놀다 drops ㄹ to become 노느라고.
im-02-02-02.why: Past tense cannot precede -느라고, and 놀다 drops its ㄹ batchim: 노느라고.

a.d: Cause must be the subject's own continuous action. The subjects of the first and second clauses must be identical.
ex: 운전**하느라고** 전화를 못 받았어요. / I couldn't answer the phone because I was driving.

b.d: Cause is an unexpected occurrence, natural event, or third party's action outside the speaker's control.
ex: 비가 오**는 바람에** 옷이 다 젖었어요. / My clothes got soaked because it rained.

im-02-02-03.tip: Ask: 'Was this my own focused action?' If yes, use -느라고. If it was an unexpected accident or weather, use -는 바람에.

im-02-02-03.q: Fix the unnatural use of -느라고 for an external weather event.
im-02-02-03.wrong: 비가 많이 오느라고 옷이 다 젖었어요.
answers: 비가 많이 오는 바람에 옷이 다 젖었어요.

im-02-02-03.hint: Rain is an uncontrollable external event, not a personal action. Use -는 바람에: 비가 많이 오는 바람에.
im-02-02-03.why: The weather is not an action the speaker performed. An external sudden cause requires -는 바람에.

a.d: Used politely in workplace or social settings to explain what pressing responsibility delayed you, followed by an apology.
ex: 자료를 검토**하느라고** 보고가 늦어졌습니다. 죄송합니다. / I apologize that my report was delayed because I was reviewing data.

b.d: If used alone without polite apology phrases (죄송합니다, 양해 부탁드립니다), it can sound like defensive excuse-making.
ex: 바쁘**느라고** 못 했어요. (✕ Grammatically incorrect & rude)

im-02-02-04.tip: In professional emails and calls, pair -느라고 with polite apologies: ~하느라고 확인이 늦었습니다. 죄송합니다.

im-02-02-04.hint: 바쁘다 is an adjective and cannot take -느라고. Use 바빠서 or an action verb like 일하느라고.
im-02-02-04.why: -느라고 only attaches to dynamic verbs, never to adjectives like 바쁘다. Use 바빠서 instead.
